title: The Last King
objective: After this level you can explain how Rome overthrew Tarquin the Proud and why it rejected kings.
summary: Tarquin the Proud ruled as a tyrant. After the Lucretia scandal, Brutus led the Romans to expel him in 509 BCE and swear off kings.

cards.headline: Rome’s kings ended with a crime, an uprising and an oath never to have another.
cards.body: The seventh king pushed too far. What came next left Romans with a lasting horror of one word: king.

cards.headline: A tyrant king
cards.body: The seventh king, Tarquin the Proud, was remembered as a tyrant who ruled by force and ignored the Senate, the very council that had begun as the king’s advisers. Then, according to tradition, the king’s son assaulted a noblewoman named Lucretia. That was the spark. The crime set off an uprising, and not just against one bad king, but against the monarchy itself.

cards.headline: No more kings
cards.body: According to tradition, the Romans, led by Lucius Junius Brutus, drove out their king in 509 BCE and ended the monarchy. Then Brutus had them swear never again to let anyone be king in Rome. Not just “no more Tarquin.” No more kings, ever.
cards.callout: The end of the monarchy: 509 BCE

cards.context: After the tyrant kings, the title rex, king, became so hated that even Rome’s most powerful later leaders avoided it. They could hold enormous power. They just couldn’t call it that.

mascot.line: Hold on to this hatred of “king.” It explains the title Augustus picks in Level 44.

cards.headline: The monarchy: ended
learned: Tarquin the Proud ruled as a tyrant
Brutus expelled the king in 509 BCE
Romans swore never to have a king again

questions.prompt: In what year, by tradition, did the Romans expel their last king?

options.label: 27 BCE
options.rationale: That’s the start of the Empire.

options.label: 476 CE
options.rationale: That’s the fall of the West.

questions.explanation: Tradition dates the expulsion of Tarquin the Proud to 509 BCE.

questions.prompt: Why did later powerful Romans avoid calling themselves king?

options.label: After the tyrant kings, the title was hated
Only priests could be called king
options.rationale: The issue was hatred of the title.

options.label: The Senate had never used the word
Kings had to be Etruscan by law

questions.explanation: After Tarquin, rex became a hated title, and Romans had sworn never to have a king again.

questions.prompt: From Level 6: which body began as the kings’ council of elders and survived their fall?
questions.explanation: The Senate began as a council advising the kings and long outlasted them.
